skill.name: designing-tests
skill.description: Designs practical testing strategies for codebases, including test type selection, templates, coverage targets, fixtures, mocks, and validation loops.
skill.summary: Guides teams through unit, integration, and end-to-end test design with coverage and validation practices.
skill.author: CloudAI-X

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are Markdown fences, documentation examples, local test code, or mock handlers. The only confirmed risk is guidance to run npm test commands, because npm scripts can execute repository-defined code. No evidence found of prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends running npm test commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit guidance to ask the user before running package-manager scripts, especially in untrusted repositories.

remediation.issue: The command examples do not mention reviewing project scripts first.
remediation.suggestion: Tell agents to inspect the configured test script and explain the command before execution.

content.value_statement: Teams often add tests without a clear coverage plan or validation loop. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through test selection, examples, mocks, and coverage checks.
actual_capabilities: Selects unit, integration, end-to-end, and component test approaches.
Recommends testing frameworks for JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go.
Provides templates for unit, integration, and end-to-end tests.
Defines coverage targets and explains what should be covered.
Guides factories, fixtures, mocks, and deterministic test data.
Includes a validation loop for test passing and coverage checks.
limitations: It does not include executable scripts or installed dependencies.
The sample commands are npm-focused and may need adaptation.
It cannot guarantee useful coverage without project context.
Domain-specific compliance tests need separate requirements.

use_cases.title: Plan New Feature Tests
use_cases.description: Create a balanced test plan before implementing or merging a feature.

use_cases.title: Improve Regression Coverage
use_cases.description: Identify missing unit, integration, and end-to-end tests for fragile areas.

use_cases.title: Standardize Test Practices
use_cases.description: Align a team around framework choices, coverage targets, mocks, and fixtures.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Test Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for test coverage ideas.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this feature and design a small test plan. Separate unit, integration, and end-to-end tests. Explain what each test should prove.

prompt_templates.title: Add Focused Unit Tests
prompt_templates.scenario: Add tests for a function, component, or module.
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect this module and propose unit tests for normal paths, edge cases, and errors. Include clear test names and required test data.

prompt_templates.title: Raise Coverage Safely
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve coverage without adding weak tests.
prompt_templates.prompt: Find meaningful coverage gaps in this area. Prioritize business logic, API contracts, and error handling before snapshots or simple accessors.

prompt_templates.title: Design a Full Test Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for a service or application.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a complete test strategy for this project. Include framework choices, fixture design, mock boundaries, coverage thresholds, flaky test risks, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Design tests for a new user registration flow.
output: Unit tests cover validation, password rules, and duplicate email handling.
Integration tests verify account creation, database writes, and error responses.
End-to-end tests cover successful signup and visible confirmation after login.

output_examples.input: Improve coverage for a payment module.
output: Prioritize business rules, failed authorization paths, refunds, and idempotency.
Use fixtures for payment states and mocks for external payment providers.
Run coverage after tests pass and review any uncovered decision branches.

output_examples.input: Choose a test stack for a TypeScript API.
output: Use Vitest for unit tests and integration tests.
Use MSW or local request helpers for API boundaries.
Add Playwright only for critical browser workflows.

best_practices: Start with business logic and API contracts before broad snapshot coverage.
Keep test data deterministic with factories, fixtures, and controlled time.
Run tests and coverage only after confirming the project command is appropriate.
anti_patterns: Do not mock the code under test instead of testing behavior.
Do not chase coverage numbers with low-value assertions.
Do not run package-manager scripts in untrusted projects without approval.

faq.question: What kinds of tests does this skill cover?
faq.answer: It covers unit, integration, end-to-end, component, and API test planning.

faq.question: Which languages are mentioned?
faq.answer: The guidance includes JavaScript, TypeScript, Python, and Go examples.

faq.question: Does it install testing tools?
faq.answer: No. It recommends frameworks and patterns but does not install dependencies.

faq.question: Does it run tests automatically?
faq.answer: It recommends validation commands, but the agent should ask before running project scripts.

faq.question: Can it help with flaky tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It highlights deterministic data, mocked time, independent tests, and repeated runs.

faq.question: Is it useful for existing projects?
faq.answer: Yes. It can review coverage gaps and propose targeted tests for risky code paths.
